additional_concerns: Neither candidate has executable meaning. Retrieval results locate passages, and the unsupported LegalRuleML result establishes no legal or executable fidelity.

Paragraph 10 establishes continuing responsibility despite outsourcing, but supplies no complete test of effective authority, supervisory discharge, incident materiality, remediation or satisfactory performance. Both candidates' proposed fulfillment tests require further justification and actual facts.

The performance candidate draws proper-records and compatibility outcomes from a separate provision. Their relevance does not establish that every operational incident automatically defeats paragraph 10 fulfillment.

Paragraph 14 directly conditions demonstration on an SFC request, while confirmation is grammatically unconditioned. Footnote 5 repeats both verbs without the request qualification; whether it inherits that qualification remains interpretive. The SFC-satisfaction standard directly attaches to demonstration; its extension to confirmation is not explicit.

Absent an SFC request, the quoted request-triggered procurement duties in paragraphs 15 and 16 do not independently arise. Continuing responsibility and proper-records duties remain. Paragraph 15 specifies operational and technical subjects; paragraph 16 instead requires a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application.

The complete paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and applicable Appendix factors are not supplied. No missing text, role overlap, supervisory standard or incident threshold should be invented. Missing evidence leaves fulfillment unresolved rather than false.
